detail.message: Detail call; reason/variation metadata has no 1:1 rewrite

dynamic-key.message: Flag key is not a static string

unbound-client.message: OpenFeature client binding not proven in scope

context-unproven.message: Cannot prove LD context -> EvaluationContext conversion

receiver-unproven.message: LaunchDarkly client expression cannot be removed safely

case.description: A bulk all-flags-state evaluation is reported as skipped with the bulk category.

A report-only call is recognized only with an argument count inside the rule's argCount range. JS boolVariationDetail takes exactly three, so two, four and a spread are unrecognized and silent. Go BoolVariationDetail takes three and the Ctx variant four (argCount plus the leading context.Context); a wrong Go count does not compile, so only the correct counts are pinned here (forked signatures are covered by the Go analyzer tests).
A detail call has no one-to-one rewrite and is reported as skipped with the detail category.
A call through an aliased SDK import is recognised and rewritten.
Two OpenFeature client bindings are visible in the same scope, so the proof is ambiguous and the call is skipped as unbound-client.
Comments between the receiver, the method name and the opening paren are hoisted in front of the rewritten call.
Block comments touching an argument move with it when the rewrite reorders the arguments (key, context, default becomes key, default, context).
Line comments after each argument of a multi-line call move with their argument, placed after the comma that follows it (Go rejects a line break before a comma).
An own-line comment above the first argument leads it, and one after the last argument goes before the closing paren.
A multi-kind or builder-made LD context cannot be converted to an EvaluationContext and is skipped as context-unproven in both languages.
A context literal with an attribute beyond key and kind would lose that attribute, so the call is skipped as context-unproven.
A context literal whose kind is not "user" would be reinterpreted as a user, so the call is skipped as context-unproven.
A default value whose type cannot be proven to match the rule's value type (a variable of unknown type) is not rewritten and is reported as default-type-unproven.
A flag key computed at runtime cannot be rewritten and is reported as dynamic-key.
A receiver that is a selector chain through a struct field is pure and never stranded (the field keeps its declaration), so the call is rewritten.

A method expression, (*ldclient.LDClient).BoolVariation(c, "k", ...), reads the key after the receiver argument, but its receiver is a type, not a proven client expression, so the call is reported as receiver-unproven and not rewritten.
A plain BoolVariation inside a function with exactly one context.Context parameter reuses that parameter as the OpenFeature context.
A parameter named context shadows the context package, so inserting context.TODO() is unsafe and the call is skipped as context-unproven.
A plain BoolVariation in a function without a context.Context parameter uses context.TODO() and adds the context import.
With two context.Context parameters in scope none is provably the right one, so a plain BoolVariation falls back to context.TODO().
A BoolVariationCtx call reuses its own first argument as the OpenFeature context and adds no import.
A receiver that is a call expression is not pure, so removing it could drop side effects; the call is skipped as receiver-unproven.
Two OpenFeature clients are fields of the same class, so the proof is ambiguous and the call is skipped as unbound-client.
A comment between the receiver and the method name has no home in the Java rewrite (only argument elements are copied), so the call is reported with no fix and left untouched.
The only OpenFeature client is a local that is reassigned, so it is not effectively final and cannot be captured by the lambda; the call is skipped as unbound-client.
The v6 LDUser overload (removed in 7.x, so this case is parsed against a stub of the v6 interface) is skipped as context-unproven.
The OpenFeature client is an instance field and the call is in a static method, where the field is not accessible; the call is skipped as unbound-client.
A boolVariation method on a user class that is not an LDClientInterface is not an SDK call, so there is no diagnostic and no rewrite.
Two rewritable calls share the ldcontext import; each fix alone leaves the import in use by the other call, and only the last remaining use removes it (batch drivers clean the rest).
A client declared alongside other bindings in a single declaration is recognised and rewritten.
Namespace imports of both SDKs (ld.init, of.OpenFeature.getClient) are proven and rewritten.
The only OpenFeature client is declared in a function that does not enclose the call, so no binding is visible and the call is skipped as unbound-client.
Multi-byte characters (an accented letter and an astral emoji) precede the call on the same line, so byte offsets and UTF-16 columns differ and the reported column must count UTF-16 code units.
Clients obtained through destructured require() of the SDK packages are proven and rewritten.
An inner-scope binding shadows the OpenFeature client name, so the rewrite is skipped as unbound-client.
When a call has both an unproven default and no OpenFeature client in scope, the earlier planner step wins (default-type-unproven comes before unbound-client).
A double-quoted static flag key is rewritten to getBooleanValue with the OpenFeature client.
A parenthesized string-literal flag key is as static as the bare literal, so it is rewritten and its fingerprint key is the literal's value in every language.
A comment inside the parentheses around a static flag key has no home (only the literal is copied), so the call is reported with no fix in every language and the source is unchanged.
A single-quoted static flag key is rewritten, keeping the surrounding await and the quote style; the SDK import is left untouched.
A function-local LaunchDarkly client whose only use is the rewritten call would be left unused, which Go rejects; the call is skipped as receiver-unproven. JS tolerates the unused local and rewrites.
Two rewritable calls on one function-local client: rewriting both would strand the local, so the planner skips every call on it, never a subset. JS rewrites both.
A template literal without expressions is a static key and is rewritten, keeping the backticks.
A client declared with an explicit LDClient type annotation is still recognised and rewritten.
Go JSONVariation takes and returns ldvalue.Value while OpenFeature ObjectValue uses any, so the call is skipped as type-mismatch.
Go IntVariation returns int while OpenFeature IntValue returns int64, so the call is skipped as type-mismatch.
A static integer flag is rewritten to getIntegerValue and unboxed with intValue to keep the primitive int.
Java jsonValueVariation takes and returns LDValue while OpenFeature getObjectValue uses Value, so the call is skipped as type-mismatch.
A static JSON flag is rewritten to getObjectValue in JS; Go JSONVariation is a separate skipped rule.
JS migrationVariation takes exactly three arguments (no callback), so two and four arguments are unrecognized and silent; only the three-argument call is reported.
A migration flag returns a stage and operation tracker rather than a plain value, so MigrationVariation(Ctx) is skipped as type-mismatch.

An int literal default widens to double for doubleVariation, but getDoubleValue(String, Double, ..) does not accept an int, so the default type is not proven and the call is skipped as default-type-unproven.
A static number flag is rewritten to getNumberValue (JS) and Go Float64Variation to FloatValue.
A null default is a String; getStringValue accepts null, so the call is rewritten.
A static string flag is rewritten to getStringValue (JS) and StringValue (Go).
JS variation takes three arguments plus an optional trailing callback (argCount 3 to 4). Two arguments, five arguments and a spread are unrecognized and silent; three and four are reported.
